dedupe_keys.name: rainwater harvesting potential maps for the united states pnnl 25498 rev 1 femp 2019

description: These two maps rank US locations by their relative potential for rainwater harvesting, one for any use and one for landscape irrigation, to help federal agencies choose sites for rainwater projects. Pacific Northwest National Laboratory produced them for the Department of Energy's Federal Energy Management Program, as a complement to its state-level rainwater harvesting regulations map; Revision 1 of report PNNL-25498 is dated June 2019. The method uses 30-year average monthly rainfall by zip code in frost-free months, counting months with at least one inch of rain, and for irrigation subtracts evapotranspiration. Coverage is the United States at zip code level. Format and access: a free 14-page PDF with maps and ranking tables. Licence: a public US federal report. Caveats: monthly averages hide storm timing and dry years, and the report gives maps, not GIS files. It supports screening of rainwater harvesting as blue infrastructure that eases stormwater runoff and drought stress. A related catalogue record is the EPA NEWR non-potable water reuse calculator.
